questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The destination. I considered doing my master's degree at this university, and this was a way to try it out.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was actually relatively easy, but there are often waiting times for responses, especially from the host university's administration. Therefore, it's crucial to remain calm, as many things only fall into place towards the end of the process.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not receive any assistance, and I did not feel that I needed it.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: If you wait until about a week or two before semester start, a lot of private accommodations halls will open up for the opportunity to a 16 weeks contract. Do no trust the university to find you something.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everybody lives off campus in Edinburgh. You do not want to live further than about 30 minutes walk from campus though.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to fill out a lot of forms, which took a long time. But it's actually quite simple—you just need to make sure you have enough time for it.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The University of Edinburgh has a very detailed guide on how everything should be filled out. They also held some online meetings where you could ask questions if there was anything you were unsure about.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted. It’s only relatively late in the process that you make your final course selections. At the University of Edinburgh, you can also change your courses after you arrive.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Find peace in the fact that many things only fall into place towards the end of the process. I have only encountered kind administrative staff at the University of Edinburgh, so just stay calm, they will help you if anything goes wrong.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses equivalent to first- and second-year levels, even though I was in the final semester of my bachelor's degree. I was really happy with my courses and would recommend others to take what are called "Level 8" courses. I found that my workload was much lighter compared to other exchange students who took higher-level courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At the University of Edinburgh, the learning approach is very self-study oriented. You spend a lot more time reading compared to the University of Copenhagen. In all three of my courses, there was a mix of lectures, which included everyone taking the course, and tutorials with around 15 people. However, lectures made up the majority of the teaching.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Trauma in Society - CNST08002
 Popular Religion, Women and Witchcraft in Early Modern Europe - DIVI08013
 Scottish Studies 1A: Conceptualising Scotland - SCET08006

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I chose three courses from three different faculties, selecting them mainly based on subjects I knew I wouldn’t be able to study in Denmark. I would particularly recommend the course "Trauma in Society - CNST08002" at the University of Edinburgh if you're interested in psychology, neurobiology, and therapy.

questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food costs are roughly the same as in Copenhagen. However, beer is really cheap—just remember to bring your student card when going out!

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There’s a club for everything! The University of Edinburgh has a very detailed program where you can visit all the clubs during the first week before classes start.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go to "Stramash" and take part in the Scottish dance ceilidh! It's a fun experience, and a great way to dive into Scottish culture!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take trips to the Highlands! I booked a guided tour to the Isle of Skye in the Highlands with other exchange students through the company "MacBackpackers". It was an amazing experience and a great way to explore the beautiful Scottish landscape

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It's really easy. Scottish culture is similar to Danish culture in many ways. Plus, there's a large international community in Edinburgh, so there's a place for everyone.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The Scots are easy to talk to, so don't be afraid to strike up a conversation

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any differences challenging

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciate the relaxed, easy-going, and helpful culture in Scotland.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Don’t live further than 30 minutes from campus. I walked every day from campus to my accommodation, and I really appreciated how easy it was to get around Edinburgh on foot, especially on weekends. Having everything within a 30-minute radius is something I miss most about Edinburgh.

2. Ask a local student to grab a coffee after class. I never did this in Denmark, but in Scotland, I did it often and made some really great connections. As an exchange student, it’s easy to end up hanging out mostly with people from your home university, but connecting with locals can really enrich your experience.

3. Plan weekend trips to the Highlands or Glasgow. You’ll likely spend most of your time in Edinburgh, so make sure to plan a weekend or two to explore the Highlands or visit Glasgow! It’s a great way to see more of Scotland and make the most of your exchange.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Create a Facebook Messenger group with the others who are also going. In our chat, we could keep track of deadlines and other practical information we had received. We also shared frustrations and gave each other good advice. We all met up once we arrived in the city, and I ended up getting a large part of my social life from that group.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: At first, it was difficult because everything was in English. Sometimes I felt like I couldn’t express myself as precisely as I wanted to. But you get used to speaking English on a daily basis, and eventually, you don’t even think about whether what you're saying sounds strange, like you might do in the beginning.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: That everything was in English.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Just do it. It is a life changing experience.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
